key_insight: Destructive many-photon interference can prevent certain false-success heralding events, improving photonic seed-state quality beyond what success probability alone reveals.
engineering_relevance: Error-resolved circuit design can reduce detector-induced output errors in entangled-state sources for linear optical quantum computing.
method: Develop a framework that separates sensitivities to physically distinct errors.
Identify seed-state generators where interference blocks false heralds caused by detector loss or noise.
Design and analyze improved Bell-state and four-qubit GHZ-state generators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports halved effective output loss for particular Bell-state generators, a new Bell generator insensitive to detector loss and noise to first order, and a 4GHZ generator with over 75% higher success probability than a standard circuit.
watch_item: First-order protection does not establish immunity to higher-order or other implementation errors; the abstract does not report experimental validation.
paper_title: Beyond Fidelity: Resolving Errors in Photonic Seed State Generation
